def iter_osm_notes(feed_limit=25, interval=60, parse_timestamps=True):
    last_seen_guid = None
    while True:
        # Open the OSM notes feed
        u = urllib2.urlopen('https://www.openstreetmap.org/api/0.6/notes/feed?limit=%d' % feed_limit)
        tree = etree.parse(u)
        new_notes = []
        
        # Iterate through each note item in the feed
        for note_item in tree.xpath('/rss/channel/item'):
            title = note_item.xpath('title')[0].text
            if title.startswith('new note ('):
                action = 'create'
            elif title.startswith('new comment ('):
                action = 'comment'
            elif title.startswith('closed note ('):
                action = 'close'
            
            # Get the GUID of the note
            guid = note_item.xpath('link')[0].text
            
            # Check if the note has already been seen
            if last_seen_guid == guid:
                break
            elif last_seen_guid is None:
                # Set the first note as the "last seen" for the first iteration
                last_seen_guid = guid
            else:
                note_id = int(guid.split('/')[-1].split('#c')[0])
                new_notes.append((action, get_note(note_id, parse_timestamps)))
        
        # Yield the new notes in reverse order (oldest to most current)
        for note in reversed(new_notes):
            yield note
        yield model.Finished(None, None)
        
        # Wait for the specified interval before checking for new notes again
        time.sleep(interval)

    now = timezone.now()
    # Filter items with no start time or start time not yet met
    queryset = queryset.filter(Q(start_time=None) | Q(start_time__lte=now))
    # Filter items with no end time or end time not yet reached

    # Calculate remaining quantity based on user's reservations
    quantity_or_zero = self._calculate_quantities(user)
    remainder = Case(
        When(limit=None, then=Value(_BIG_QUANTITY)),
        default=F("limit") - Sum(quantity_or_zero),

def _autoextend_reservation(self):
    # Calculate the time elapsed since the cart was last updated
    time = timezone.now()
    time_elapsed_since_updated = time - self.cart.time_last_updated
    
    # Calculate the residual reservation duration
    residual = self.cart.reservation_duration - time_elapsed_since_updated
    reservations = [datetime.timedelta(0), residual]
    
    # If there are vouchers, add a minimum reservation duration
    if len(self.cart.vouchers.all()) >= 1:
        reservations.append(inventory.Voucher.RESERVATION_DURATION)
    
    # If there are products in the cart, add the maximum reservation duration of those products
    items = commerce.ProductItem.objects.filter(cart=self.cart)
    agg = items.aggregate(Max("product__reservation_duration"))
    product_max = agg["product__reservation_duration__max"]
    if product_max is not None:
        reservations.append(product_max)
    
    # Update the cart's last updated time and reservation duration
    self.cart.time_last_updated = time
    self.cart.reservation_duration = max(reservations)

def fix_simple_errors(self):
    # Remove invalid vouchers from the cart
    to_remove = []
    for voucher in self.cart.vouchers.all():
        try:
            self._test_voucher(voucher)
        except ValidationError:
            to_remove.append(voucher)
    for voucher in to_remove:
        self.cart.vouchers.remove(voucher)

    # Fix product and discount quantities
    items = commerce.ProductItem.objects.filter(cart=self.cart).select_related("product")
    products = set(i.product for i in items)
    available = set(ProductController.available_products(self.cart.user, products=products))
    not_available = products - available
    zeros = [(product, 0) for product in not_available]
    self.set_quantities(zeros)

def sales_payment_summary():
    # Helper function to get a value from an aggregate or return 0 if the key is missing
    def value_or_zero(aggregate, key):
        return aggregate.get(key, 0)

    # Helper function to sum the 'amount' field from a set of payments
    def sum_amount(payment_set):
        a = payment_set.values("amount").aggregate(total=Sum("amount"))
        return value_or_zero(a, "total")

    # Define the headings for the report
    headings = ["Category", "Total"]
    data = []

    # Summarize all sales made (income)
    sales = commerce.LineItem.objects.filter(invoice__status=commerce.Invoice.STATUS_PAID).values("price", "quantity").aggregate(total=Sum(F("price") * F("quantity"), output_field=CURRENCY()))
    sales = value_or_zero(sales, "total")

    # Summarize all payments
    all_payments = sum_amount(commerce.PaymentBase.objects.all())

    # Calculate various credit note-related values
    all_credit_notes = 0 - sum_amount(commerce.CreditNote.objects.all())
    unclaimed_credit_notes = 0 - sum_amount(commerce.CreditNote.unclaimed())
    claimed_credit_notes = sum_amount(commerce.CreditNoteApplication.objects.all())
    refunded_credit_notes = 0 - sum_amount(commerce.CreditNote.refunded())

    # Append data to the report
    data.append(["Items on paid invoices", sales])
    data.append(["All payments", all_payments])
    data.append(["Sales - Payments", sales - all_payments])
    data.append(["All credit notes", all_credit_notes])
    data.append(["Credit notes paid on invoices", claimed_credit_notes])
    data.append(["Credit notes refunded", refunded_credit_notes])
    data.append(["Unclaimed credit notes", unclaimed_credit_notes])
    data.append(["Credit notes - (claimed credit notes + unclaimed credit notes)", all_credit_notes - claimed_credit_notes - refunded_credit_notes - unclaimed_credit_notes])

    # Return the report
    return ListReport("Sales and Payments Summary", headings, data)

def _handle_products(request, category, products, prefix):

    current_cart = CartController.for_user(request.user)
    
    # Create a form for handling products
    ProductsForm = forms.ProductsForm(category, products)
    
    # Initialize quantities for products in the cart
    items = commerce.ProductItem.objects.filter(product__in=products, cart=current_cart.cart).select_related("product")
    quantities = []
    seen = set()
    for item in items:
        quantities.append((item.product, item.quantity))
        seen.add(item.product)
    
    # Add products not in the cart with a quantity of 0
    zeros = set(products) - seen
    for product in zeros:
        quantities.append((product, 0))
    
    # Create the products form with initial quantities
    products_form = ProductsForm(request.POST or None, product_quantities=quantities, prefix=prefix)
    
    # Handle form submission
    if request.method == "POST" and products_form.is_valid():
        if products_form.has_changed():
            _set_quantities_from_products_form(products_form, current_cart)
        
        # Check if category is required and user has at least one item in the cart
        if category.required:

                products_form.add_error(None, "You must have at least one item from this category")

    handled = False if products_form.errors else True

def available_discounts(cls, user, categories, products):
    # Filter clauses based on user, categories, and products
    filtered_clauses = cls._filtered_clauses(user)
    categories = set(categories)
    products = set(products)
    
    # Determine product categories
    product_categories = set(product.category for product in products)
    all_categories = categories | product_categories
    
    # Filter clauses based on product and category matches
    filtered_clauses = (
        clause for clause in filtered_clauses 
        if (hasattr(clause, 'product') and clause.product in products) 
        or (hasattr(clause, 'category') and clause.category in all_categories)
    )
    
    # Initialize sets to track accepted and failed discounts
    discounts = []
    accepted_discounts = set()
    failed_discounts = set()
    
    # Evaluate each clause
    for clause in filtered_clauses:
        discount = clause.discount
        cond = ConditionController.for_condition(discount)
        past_use_count = clause.past_use_count
        
        # Check if the clause has exceeded its use count
        if past_use_count >= clause.quantity:
            continue
        
        # Check if the discount is still available
        if discount not in failed_discounts:
            is_accepted = discount in accepted_discounts
            
            # Check if the clause is valid for the user
            if is_accepted or cond.is_met(user, filtered=True):
                discounts.append(DiscountAndQuantity(discount=discount, clause=clause, quantity=clause.quantity - past_use_count))
                accepted_discounts.add(discount)
            else:
                failed_discounts.add(discount)
    
    return discounts

def _annotate_with_past_uses(cls, queryset, user):
    """
    Annotates the queryset with the count of past uses of discounts for either a category or a product by a specific user.

    Args:
        cls: The class containing the method.
        queryset: The queryset to be annotated.
        user: The user for whom to count past uses.

    Returns:
        The annotated queryset with an additional field 'past_use_count' representing the total past use quantity.
    """
    if queryset.model == conditions.DiscountForCategory:
        matches = Q(category=F('discount__discountitem__product__category'))
    elif queryset.model == conditions.DiscountForProduct:
        matches = Q(product=F('discount__discountitem__product'))

    in_carts = Q(discount__discountitem__cart__user=user) & Q(discount__discountitem__cart__status=commerce.Cart.STATUS_PAID)

    past_use_quantity = When(in_carts & matches, then="discount__discountitem__quantity")

def _generate_from_cart(cls, cart):
    # Refresh the cart from the database
    cart.refresh_from_db()
    
    # Filter and select related product items
    product_items = commerce.ProductItem.objects.filter(cart=cart).select_related("product", "product__category").order_by("product__category__order", "product__order")
    
    # Raise an error if the cart is empty
    if len(product_items) == 0:
        raise ValidationError("Your cart is empty.")
    
    # Filter and select related discount items
    discount_items = commerce.DiscountItem.objects.filter(cart=cart).select_related("discount", "product", "product__category")
    
    # Format product description
    def format_product(product):
        return "%s - %s" % (product.category.name, product.name)
    
    # Format discount description
    def format_discount(discount, product):
        description = discount.description
        return "%s (%s)" % (description, format_product(product))
    
    # Create line items for product items
    line_items = []
    for item in product_items:
        product = item.product
        line_item = commerce.LineItem(description=format_product(product), quantity=item.quantity, price=product.price, product=product)
        line_items.append(line_item)
    
    # Create line items for discount items
    for item in discount_items:
        line_item = commerce.LineItem(description=format_discount(item.discount, item.product), quantity=item.quantity, price=cls.resolve_discount_value(item) * -1, product=item.product)
        line_items.append(line_item)
    
    # Generate the invoice
    min_due_time = cart.reservation_duration + cart.time_last_updated
    return cls._generate(cart.user, cart, min_due_time, line_items)

def _upload_file(self, fn):
    # Get the size of the file and generate a session ID
    size = os.path.getsize(fn)
    counter = 0
    base_name = os.path.basename(fn)
    session_id = str(uuid.uuid4())

    # Open the file in binary read mode
    with open(fn, 'rb') as f:
        while True:
            response = None
            chunk = f.read(CHUNK_SIZE)
            if not chunk:
                break

            # Retry uploading the chunk up to 5 times
            for i in range(5):
                content_range = 'bytes {}-{}/{}'.format(counter * CHUNK_SIZE, counter * CHUNK_SIZE + len(chunk) - 1, size)
                if i > 0 and response is not None:
                    print("Chunk upload failed (error {}): repeating {}".format(response.status_code, content_range))

                response = requests.post(urlparse.urljoin(self.url, 'upload/'), auth=self.auth, data=chunk, headers={
                    'Content-Disposition': 'attachment; filename="{}"'.format(base_name),
                    'Content-Length': size,
                    'Content-Range': content_range,
                    'Content-Type': 'application/octet-stream',
                    'Session-Id': session_id
                })

                if response.status_code in [200, 201]:
                    break

            # If all retries fail, return None
            if response.status_code not in [200, 201]:
                return None

            # Update progress and print it
            progress = 100. * (counter * CHUNK_SIZE + len(chunk)) / size
            sys.stdout.write("\r{:.0f} % Uploading {}".format(progress, fn))
            sys.stdout.flush()
            counter += 1

    print()
    return session_id

def search_variants_by_coordinates(coordinate_query, search_mode='any'):
    """
    Searches for variants within a specified coordinate range and returns their digests based on the search mode.

    Parameters:
    coordinate_query (object): An object containing the start, stop, chr, and alt attributes.
    search_mode (str): The mode of search, can be 'any', 'include_smaller', 'include_larger', or 'exact'.

    Returns:
    list: A list of variant digests that match the search criteria.
    """
    ct = COORDINATE_TABLE
    chr_idx = COORDINATE_TABLE_CHR
    start_idx = COORDINATE_TABLE_START
    stop_idx = COORDINATE_TABLE_STOP

    start = int(coordinate_query.start)
    stop = int(coordinate_query.stop)
    chromosome = str(coordinate_query.chr)

    left_idx = chr_idx.searchsorted(chromosome)
    right_idx = chr_idx.searchsorted(chromosome, side='right')
    chr_ct_idx = chr_idx[left_idx:right_idx].index

    left_idx = start_idx.searchsorted(start)
    right_idx = start_idx.searchsorted(stop, side='right')
    start_ct_idx = start_idx[:right_idx].index

    left_idx = stop_idx.searchsorted(start)
    stop_ct_idx = stop_idx[left_idx:].index

    match_idx = chr_ct_idx & start_ct_idx & stop_ct_idx
    m_df = ct.loc[match_idx,]

    if search_mode == 'any':
        var_digests = m_df.v_hash.to_list()
        return [CACHE[v] for v in var_digests]
    elif search_mode == 'include_smaller':
        match_idx = (start <= m_df.start) & (stop >= m_df.stop)
    elif search_mode == 'include_larger':
        match_idx = (start >= m_df.start) & (stop <= m_df.stop)
    elif search_mode == 'exact':
        match_idx = (start == m_df.stop) & (stop == m_df.start)
    else:
        raise ValueError("unexpected search mode")

    if coordinate_query.alt:
        match_idx = match_idx & (coordinate_query.alt == m_df.alt)

    var_digests = m_df.loc[match_idx,].v_hash.to_list()
    return [CACHE[v] for v in var_digests]

def calcPF(pf):
    pf_y = pf[:1]
    pf_x = pf[1:]
    result = 100
    if pf_y == CosTheta.CapacitiveLead:
        result = 200 - int(pf_x)
    elif pf_y == CosTheta.InductiveLag:
        result = int(pf_x)
    return result

If `pf_y` matches `CosTheta.CapacitiveLead`, it calculates `result` as 200 minus the integer value of `pf_x`. If `pf_y` matches `CosTheta.InductiveLag`, it sets `result` to the integer value of `pf_x`. Finally, it returns the calculated `result`.

        self.setContext("")
        return False

def requestA(self):
    # Save the current context
    work_context = self.getContext()
    
    # Set the context to "request[v4A]"
    self.setContext("request[v4A]")
    
    # Send a request to the meter
    self.m_serial_port.write("2f3f".decode("hex") + self.m_meter_address + "3030210d0a".decode("hex"))
    
    # Get the raw response from the meter
    self.m_raw_read_a = self.m_serial_port.getResponse(self.getContext())
    
    # Unpack the raw response using the structure defined in m_blk_a
    unpacked_read_a = self.unpackStruct(self.m_raw_read_a, self.m_blk_a)
    
    # Convert the unpacked data using the structure defined in m_blk_a
    self.convertData(unpacked_read_a, self.m_blk_a)
    
    # Extract the kWh precision from the unpacked data
    self.m_kwh_precision = int(self.m_blk_a[Field.kWh_Scale][MeterData.NativeValue])
    
    # Calculate the CRC for the meter read
    self.m_a_crc = self.crcMeterRead(self.m_raw_read_a, self.m_blk_a)
    
    # Restore the original context
    self.setContext(work_context)
    
    # Return the calculated CRC
    return self.m_a_crc

def checker(location, receiver):
    path = filepath.FilePath(location)
    files = set()
    filesContents = {}

    def _check(path):
        currentFiles = set(fname for fname in os.listdir(location) if not fname.endswith('.new'))
        removed = files - currentFiles
        added = currentFiles - files

        for fname in added:
            contents = path.child(fname).getContent()
            filesContents[fname] = contents
            receiver.add(fname, contents)

        for fname in removed:
            receiver.remove(fname)

        same = currentFiles & files
        for fname in same:
            newContents = path.child(fname).getContent()
            oldContents = filesContents[fname]
            if newContents == oldContents:
                continue
            receiver.remove(fname)
            filesContents[fname] = newContents
            receiver.add(fname, newContents)

        files.clear()
        files.update(currentFiles)

    return functools.partial(_check, path)

def runProcess(args, timeout, grace, reactor):
    deferred = defer.Deferred()
    protocol = ProcessProtocol(deferred)
    process = reactor.spawnProcess(protocol, args[0], args, env=os.environ)

    def _logEnded(err):
        err.trap(tierror.ProcessDone, tierror.ProcessTerminated)
        print(err.value)
    deferred.addErrback(_logEnded)

    def _cancelTermination(dummy):
        for termination in terminations:
            if termination.active():
                termination.cancel()
    deferred.addCallback(_cancelTermination)

    terminations = []
    terminations.append(reactor.callLater(timeout, process.signalProcess, "TERM"))
    terminations.append(reactor.callLater(timeout + grace, process.signalProcess, "KILL"))

    return deferred

def check(settings, states, location):
    # Create a dictionary of children with their basenames as keys
    children = {child.basename(): child for child in location.children()}
    
    # Initialize sets for last, current, gone, and added states
    last = set(states)
    current = set(children)
    gone = last - current
    added = current - last
    
    # Close and remove states that are no longer present
    for name in gone:
        states[name].close()
        del states[name]
    
    # Add new states for children that are newly present
    for name in added:
        states[name] = State(location=children[name], settings=settings)
    
    # Return a list of names of states that pass the check
    return [name for name, state in six.iteritems(states) if state.check()]

def descendant(self, chain_path):
    # Initialize the public child with the HD keychain
    public_child = self.hdkeychain
    
    # Define the number of bytes per step and the maximum bits per step
    chain_step_bytes = 4
    max_bits_per_step = 2 ** 31
    
    # Split the chain path into steps and convert each step to an integer
    chain_steps = [
        int(chain_path[i:i + chain_step_bytes * 2], 16) % max_bits_per_step
        for i in range(0, len(chain_path), chain_step_bytes * 2)
    ]
    
    # Iterate through each step and get the child public key
    for step in chain_steps:
        public_child = public_child.get_child(step)
    
    # Return the final public key chain
    return PublicKeychain(public_child)

def nth_child_production(self, lexeme, tokens):
    # Match the 'expr' pattern from the tokens
    args = self.match(tokens, 'expr')
    # Use a regular expression to parse the matched arguments
    pat = self.nth_child_pat.match(args)
    
    # Determine the values of 'a' and 'b' based on the parsed pattern
    if pat.group(5):
        a = 2
        b = 1 if pat.group(5) == 'odd' else 0
    elif pat.group(6):
        a = 0
        b = int(pat.group(6))
    else:
        sign = pat.group(1) or '+'
        coef = pat.group(2) or '1'
        a = eval(sign + coef)
        b = eval(pat.group(3) + pat.group(4)) if pat.group(3) else 0
    
    # Determine if the selection should be reversed
    reverse = lexeme == 'nth-last-child'
    
    # Define a validation function to check if a node matches the nth-child pattern
    def validate(node):
        if not node.siblings:
            return False
        idx = node.idx - 1
        tot = node.siblings
        if reverse:
            idx = tot - idx
        else:
            idx += 1
        
        if a == 0:
            m = b == idx
        else:
            mod = (idx - b) % a
            m = not mod and (idx * a + b) >= 0
        
        return m
    
    return validate

def chain_check(cls, timestamp: int) -> bool:
    # Retrieve the record for the given timestamp
    record = cls.get_record(timestamp)
    
    # Check if the record is an instance of NistBeaconValue
    if not isinstance(record, NistBeaconValue):
        return False
    
    # Retrieve the previous and next records
    prev_record = cls.get_previous(record.timestamp)
    next_record = cls.get_next(record.timestamp)
    
    # Check if both previous and next records are None
    if prev_record is None and next_record is None:
        return False
    
    # Check if both previous and next records are instances of NistBeaconValue
    if isinstance(prev_record, NistBeaconValue) and isinstance(next_record, NistBeaconValue):
        # Check if all records have proper signatures and the previous output values match
        return (record.valid_signature and prev_record.valid_signature and next_record.valid_signature and
                record.previous_output_value == prev_record.output_value and
                next_record.previous_output_value == record.output_value)
    
    # Check if only the next record is an instance of NistBeaconValue (potential first record)
    if prev_record is None and isinstance(next_record, NistBeaconValue):
        # Check if the record has a proper signature, the next record has a proper signature,
        # the record is the initial record, and the next record's previous output value matches
        return (record.valid_signature and next_record.valid_signature and
                cls._INIT_RECORD == record and
                next_record.previous_output_value == record.output_value)
    
    # Check if only the previous record is an instance of NistBeaconValue (potential last record)
    if isinstance(prev_record, NistBeaconValue) and next_record is None:
        # Check if the record has a proper signature, the previous record has a proper signature,
        # and the record's previous output value matches
        return (record.valid_signature and prev_record.valid_signature and
                record.previous_output_value == prev_record.output_value)

def _parse_format(self, format):
    # Strip leading/trailing whitespace and replace multiple spaces with a single space
    format = re.sub(r'[ \t]+', ' ', format.strip())
    subpatterns = []
    
    # Regular expressions for various patterns
    findquotes = re.compile(r'^\\"')
    findreferreragent = re.compile(r'Referer|User-Agent')
    findpercent = re.compile(r'^%.*t$')
    lstripquotes = re.compile(r'^\\"')
    rstripquotes = re.compile(r'\\"$')
    header = re.compile(r'.*%\{([^\}]+)\}i')
    
    # Split the format string by spaces
    for element in format.split(' '):
        hasquotes = 1 if findquotes.search(element) else 0
        
        # Remove leading/trailing quotes if present
        if hasquotes:
            element = lstripquotes.sub('', element)
            element = rstripquotes.sub('', element)
        
        # Check if the element matches a header pattern
        head = header.match(element)
        if head:
            self._names.append(head.groups()[0].lower())
            self._types.append(str)
        else:
            self._names.append(self.alias(element))
            self._types.append(self.types.get(element, [None, str])[1])
        
        # Determine the subpattern based on the element
        subpattern = '(\S*)'
        if hasquotes:
            if element == '%r' or findreferreragent.search(element):
                subpattern = r'\"([^"\\]*(?:\\.[^"\\]*)*)\"'
            else:
                subpattern = r'\"([^\"]*)\"'
        elif findpercent.search(element):
            subpattern = r'(\[[^\]]+\])'
        elif element == '%U':
            subpattern = '(.+?)'
        
        subpatterns.append(subpattern)
    
    # Join subpatterns to form the final pattern and compile it
    self._pattern = '^' + ' '.join(subpatterns) + '$'
    try:
        self._regex = re.compile(self._pattern)
    except Exception as e:
        raise ApacheLogParserError(e)

def createClient(self):
    # Retrieve configuration settings
    server = self.config.get('server', 'localhost')
    port = self.config.get('port', 5555)
    failover = self.config.get('failover', False)
    
    # Create a Riemann client factory
    self.factory = riemann.RiemannClientFactory(server, failover=failover)
    
    # Determine the initial server to connect to
    if failover:
        initial = random.choice(server)
    else:
        initial = server
    
    # Log the connection attempt
    log.msg(f'Connecting to Riemann on {initial}:{port}')
    
    # Establish the connection based on TLS support
    if self.tls:
        if SSL:
            self.connector = reactor.connectSSL(initial, port, self.factory, ClientTLSContext(self.key, self.cert))
        else:
            log.msg('[FATAL] SSL support not available! Please install PyOpenSSL. Exiting now')
            reactor.stop()
    else:
        self.connector = reactor.connectTCP(initial, port, self.factory)
    
    # Wait for the connection to be established
    d = defer.Deferred()
    def cb():
        if hasattr(self.factory, 'proto') and self.factory.proto:
            self.t.start(self.inter)
            d.callback(None)
        else:
            reactor.callLater(0.01, cb)
    cb()
    return d

def r_q_send(self, msg_dict):
    # Check if msg_dict can be pickled
    no_pickle_keys = self.invalid_dict_pickle_keys(msg_dict)
    if no_pickle_keys == []:
        self.r_q.put(msg_dict)
    else:
        # Handle pickle error
        hash_func = md5()
        hash_func.update(str(msg_dict))
        dict_hash = str(hash_func.hexdigest())[-7:]
        linesep = os.linesep
        sys.stderr.write(f"{datetime.now()} {Style.BRIGHT}r_q_send({dict_hash}) Can't pickle this dict:{Style.RESET_ALL} '''{msg_dict}''' {linesep}")
        
        # List of offending keys
        err_frag1 = f"{Style.BRIGHT}    r_q_send({dict_hash}) Offending dict keys:{Style.RESET_ALL}"
        err_frag2 = f" {no_pickle_keys}"
        sys.stderr.write(err_frag1 + err_frag2 + linesep)
        for key in sorted(no_pickle_keys):
            sys.stderr.write(f"      msg_dict['{key}']: {Fore.MAGENTA}{repr(msg_dict.get(key))}{Style.RESET_ALL}{linesep}")
            
            # Check for offending attributes if the value is an object
            if isinstance(msg_dict.get(key), object):
                no_pickle_attrs = self.invalid_obj_pickle_attrs(msg_dict.get(key))
                err_frag1 = f"{Style.BRIGHT}      r_q_send({dict_hash}) Offending attrs:{Style.RESET_ALL}"
                err_frag2 = f" {no_pickle_attrs}"
                sys.stderr.write(err_frag1 + err_frag2 + linesep)
                for attr in no_pickle_attrs:
                    sys.stderr.write(f"        msg_dict['{key}'].{attr}: {Fore.RED}{repr(getattr(msg_dict.get(key), attr))}{Style.RESET_ALL}{linesep}")
        
        # List of keys with no problems
        sys.stderr.write(f"{Style.BRIGHT}    r_q_send({dict_hash}) keys (no problems):{Style.RESET_ALL}{linesep}")
        for key in sorted(set(msg_dict.keys()).difference(no_pickle_keys)):
            sys.stderr.write(f"      msg_dict['{key}']: {Fore.GREEN}{repr(msg_dict.get(key))}{Style.RESET_ALL}{linesep}")

def call(args, stdout=None, stderr=None, stdin=None, daemonize=False, preexec_fn=None, shell=False, cwd=None, env=None):
    # Define a lambda function to handle stream redirection
    stream = lambda s, m: s is None and os.open(os.devnull, m) or s
    
    # Redirect stdout, stderr, and stdin
    stdout = stream(stdout, os.O_WRONLY)
    stderr = stream(stderr, os.O_WRONLY)
    stdin = stream(stdin, os.O_RDONLY)
    
    # Create a shared memory value for the child process ID
    shared_pid = Value('i', 0)
    
    # Fork the process
    pid = os.fork()
    
    if pid > 0:
        # Parent process
        os.waitpid(pid, 0)
        child_pid = shared_pid.value
        del shared_pid
        
        if daemonize:
            sys.exit(0)
        
        return child_pid
    else:
        # Child process
        os.setsid()
        
        # Create a subprocess with the provided arguments and configurations
        proc = subprocess.Popen(args, stdout=stdout, stderr=stderr, stdin=stdin, close_fds=True, preexec_fn=preexec_fn, shell=shell, cwd=cwd, env=env)
        
        # Set the child process ID in shared memory
        shared_pid.value = proc.pid
        
        # Exit the child process
        os._exit(0)

def _mkdir(p):
    # Get the absolute path of the input directory
    p = os.path.abspath(p)
    # Initialize a stack with the absolute path
    stack = [p]
    # Loop until the current path is a directory
    while not os.path.isdir(stack[-1]):
        # Get the parent directory of the current path
        parent_dir = os.path.dirname(stack[-1])
        # Append the parent directory to the stack
        stack.append(parent_dir)
    # Loop through the stack and create directories
    while stack:
        p = stack.pop()
        # If the current path is not a directory, create it
        if not os.path.isdir(p):
            os.mkdir(p)

    # Return an instance of the class with the original and authenticated requests
    return cls(request, authenticated_request)

    cmd = f"docker run --log-driver=none --rm -v {work_dir}:/data quay.io/ucsc_cgl/samtools view -f66 {os.path.join(work_dir, bam_name)}"
    process = subprocess.Popen(args=cmd, shell=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
    
    b_sum = 0.0
    b_count = 0.0
    
    # Read the output line by line
    while True:
        line = process.stdout.readline()
        if not line:
            break
        tmp = line.split("\t")
        # Check if the insert size is less than 10,000
        if abs(long(tmp[8])) < 10000:
            b_sum += abs(long(tmp[8]))
            b_count += 1
    
    process.wait()
    
    # Calculate the mean insert size
    try:
        mean = b_sum / b_count
    except ZeroDivisionError:
        mean = 150
    
    print("Using insert size: %d" % mean)
    return int(mean)

    empty_config = wrapper.__get_empty_config()
    config_yaml = ruamel.yaml.load(empty_config)
    wrapper.__populate_parser_from_config(arg_parser, config_yaml)
    args = arg_parser.parse_args()
    
    # Update the configuration YAML with parsed arguments
    for k, v in vars(args).items():
        k = k.replace('_', '-')
        if k in config_yaml:

    # Save the updated configuration YAML to a file

def __populate_parser_from_config(self, arg_parser, config_data, prefix=''):
    """
    Recursively populates an argument parser with options from a configuration dictionary.

    Args:
        arg_parser (argparse.ArgumentParser): The argument parser to populate.
        config_data (dict): The configuration dictionary containing options.
        prefix (str, optional): A prefix to prepend to option names. Defaults to ''.

    Returns:
        None
    """
    for k, v in config_data.items():
        k = prefix + '.' + k if prefix else k
        if isinstance(v, dict):
            self.__populate_parser_from_config(arg_parser, v, prefix=k)
        else:
            self._add_option(arg_parser, name=k, default=v)

def _get_mount_path(self):
    if self._mount_path is None:
        name = current_docker_container_id()
        if dockerd_is_reachable():
            blob = json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['docker', 'inspect', name]))
            mounts = blob[0]['Mounts']
            sock_mnt = [x['Source'] == x['Destination'] for x in mounts if 'docker.sock' in x['Source']]
            require(len(sock_mnt) == 1, 'Missing socket mount. Requires the following: docker run -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock')
            if len(mounts) == 2:
                require(all(x['Source'] == x['Destination'] for x in mounts), 'Docker Src/Dst mount points, invoked with the -v argument, must be the same if only using one mount point aside from the docker socket.')
                work_mount = [x['Source'] for x in mounts if 'docker.sock' not in x['Source']]
            else:
                mirror_mounts = [x['Source'] for x in mounts if x['Source'] == x['Destination']]
                work_mount = [x for x in mirror_mounts if 'docker.sock' not in x]
                require(len(work_mount) == 1, 'Wrong number of mirror mounts provided, see documentation.')
            self._mount_path = work_mount[0]
            log.info('The work mount is: %s', self._mount_path)
        else:
            raise UserError('Docker daemon is not reachable, ensure Docker is being run with: "-v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock" as an argument.')
    return self._mount_path

def get_user_affinity(self, test):
    # Create a temporary view for the test data
    test.createOrReplaceTempView(self.f("{prefix}df_test"))
    
    # Select distinct users from the test data and cluster by user
    query = self.f("SELECT DISTINCT {col_user} FROM {prefix}df_test CLUSTER BY {col_user}")
    df_test_users = self.spark.sql(query)
    
    # Save the distinct users back to a table
    df_test_users.write.mode("overwrite").saveAsTable(self.f("{prefix}df_test_users"))
    
    # Join the training data with the distinct users to get user-item ratings
    query = self.f("""
        SELECT a.{col_user}, a.{col_item}, CAST(a.{col_rating} AS double) {col_rating}
        FROM {prefix}df_train a INNER JOIN {prefix}df_test_users b ON a.{col_user} = b.{col_user} 
        DISTRIBUTE BY {col_user}
        SORT BY {col_user}, {col_item}          
    """)
    return self.spark.sql(query)

def subscribe(self, stream, callback, transform=""):
    if self.status in ["disconnected", "disconnecting", "connecting"]:
        self.connect()
    if self.status != "connected":
        return False
    logging.debug("Subscribing to %s", stream)
    self.send({"cmd": "subscribe", "arg": stream, "transform": transform})
    with self.subscription_lock:
        self.subscriptions[stream + ":" + transform] = callback
    return True

def connect(self):
    # Wait for the lock to be available
    self.ws_openlock.acquire()
    self.ws_openlock.release()

    if self.status == "connected":
        return True  # Already connected

    if self.status == "disconnecting":
        # If currently disconnecting, wait a moment, and retry
        time.sleep(0.1)
        return self.connect()

    if self.status == "disconnected" or self.status == "reconnecting":
        # Create a WebSocketApp and start a new thread to run it
        self.ws = websocket.WebSocketApp(self.ws_url, header=self.headers,
                                          on_message=self.__on_message,
                                          on_ping=self.__on_ping,
                                          on_open=self.__on_open,
                                          on_close=self.__on_close,
                                          on_error=self.__on_error)
        self.ws_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.ws.run_forever)
        self.ws_thread.daemon = True
        self.status = "connecting"
        self.ws_openlock.acquire()
        self.ws_thread.start()
        self.ws_openlock.release()

    return self.status == "connected"

def __reconnect(self):
    # Reset the status to "reconnecting"
    self.status = "reconnecting"
    
    # Calculate the reconnect time based on the time since disconnection
    if self.disconnected_time - self.connected_time > 15 * 60:
        self.reconnect_time = self.reconnect_time_starting_seconds
    else:
        self.reconnect_time *= self.reconnect_time_backoff_multiplier
    
    # Cap the reconnect time at the maximum allowed time
    if self.reconnect_time > self.reconnect_time_max_seconds:
        self.reconnect_time = self.reconnect_time_max_seconds
    
    # Add randomness to the reconnect time to avoid overwhelming the server
    self.reconnect_time *= 1 + random.uniform(-0.2, 0.2)
    
    # Ensure the reconnect time is not less than the starting time
    if self.reconnect_time < self.reconnect_time_starting_seconds:
        self.reconnect_time = self.reconnect_time_starting_seconds
    
    # Log the reconnect attempt and start a timer to perform the reconnect
    logging.warn("ConnectorDB:WS: Attempting to reconnect in %fs", self.reconnect_time)
    self.reconnector = threading.Timer(self.reconnect_time, self.__reconnect_fnc)
    self.reconnector.daemon = True
    self.reconnector.start()

def base_tokenizer(fp):
    if isinstance(fp, StringIO):
        template_file = fp
        size = template_file.len
    else:
        if os.fstat(fp.fileno()).st_size == 0:
            yield TOKEN_EOF, 'EOF', 0, 0
            return
        template_file = mmap.mmap(fp.fileno(), 0, access=mmap.ACCESS_READ)
        size = template_file.size()
        lineno = 0

    while True:
        lineno += 1
        pos = 1
        if template_file.tell() == size:
            yield TOKEN_EOF, 'EOF', lineno, 0
            break

        line = template_file.readline().decode('utf-8')
        line = line.replace('\r\n', '').replace('\n', '')

        if re_comment.match(line):
            continue

        last_text = deque()
        while line:
            line_len = len(line)
            for token in tokens:
                m = token.regex.match(line)
                if m:
                    if last_text:
                        yield TOKEN_TEXT, ''.join(last_text), lineno, pos
                        pos += len(last_text)
                        last_text.clear()
                    offset, value = m.end(), m.group()
                    line = line[offset:]
                    yield token, value, lineno, pos
                    pos += offset
                    break
            if line_len == len(line):
                last_text.append(line[0])
                line = line[1:]
            if last_text:
                yield TOKEN_TEXT, ''.join(last_text), lineno, pos
                pos += len(last_text)
                last_text.clear()
            yield TOKEN_NEWLINE, '\n', lineno, pos

    template_file.close()

def next_generation(self, mut_rate=0, max_mut_amt=0, log_base=10):
    # Check if parallel processing is enabled
    if self.__num_processes > 1:
        process_pool = Pool(processes=self.__num_processes)
        members = [m.get() for m in self.__members]
    else:
        members = self.__members
    
    # Raise an exception if no members are found
    if len(members) == 0:
        raise Exception('Generation 0 not found: use generate_population() first')
    
    # Select members for reproduction
    selected_members = self.__select_fn(members)
    
    # Calculate reproduction probabilities
    reproduction_probs = list(reversed(logspace(0.0, 1.0, num=len(selected_members), base=log_base)))
    reproduction_probs /= sum(reproduction_probs)
    
    # Initialize the next generation members list
    self.__members = []
    
    # Create the next generation members
    for _ in range(self.__pop_size):
        parent_1 = nrandom.choice(selected_members, p=reproduction_probs)
        parent_2 = nrandom.choice(selected_members, p=reproduction_probs)
        
        # Create a feed dictionary for the new member
        feed_dict = {}
        for param in self.__parameters:
            which_parent = uniform(0, 1)
            if which_parent < 0.5:
                feed_dict[param.name] = parent_1.parameters[param.name]
            else:
                feed_dict[param.name] = parent_2.parameters[param.name]
            
            # Mutate the parameter if mutation rate is greater than 0
            if mut_rate > 0:
                feed_dict[param.name] = self.__mutate_parameter(feed_dict[param.name], param, mut_rate, max_mut_amt)
        
        # Add the new member to the process pool or directly to the members list
        if self.__num_processes > 1:
            self.__members.append(process_pool.apply_async(self._start_process, [self.__cost_fn, feed_dict, self.__cost_fn_args]))
        else:
            self.__members.append(Member(feed_dict, self.__cost_fn(feed_dict, self.__cost_fn_args)))
    
    # Close and join the process pool if parallel processing is enabled
    if self.__num_processes > 1:
        process_pool.close()
        process_pool.join()
    
    # Determine the best member in the new generation
    self.__determine_best_member()

    # Set the read position past the BOM if one was found, otherwise set it to the start of the stream
    self.rawStream.seek(encoding and seek or 0)

def get_current_traceback(ignore_system_exceptions=False, show_hidden_frames=False, skip=0):
    """
    Retrieves the current traceback information.

    Args:
        ignore_system_exceptions (bool): If True, system exceptions are ignored.
        show_hidden_frames (bool): If False, hidden frames are filtered out.
        skip (int): Number of frames to skip in the traceback.

    Returns:
        Traceback: The current traceback object.
    """
    exc_type, exc_value, tb = sys.exc_info()
    if ignore_system_exceptions and exc_type in system_exceptions:
        raise
    for _ in range(skip):
        if tb.tb_next is None:
            break
        tb = tb.tb_next
    tb = Traceback(exc_type, exc_value, tb)
    if not show_hidden_frames:
        tb.filter_hidden_frames()
    return tb

def make_path_relative(path, rel_to):
    # Extract the filename and normalize the paths
    path_filename = os.path.basename(path)
    path = os.path.normpath(os.path.abspath(path))
    rel_to = os.path.normpath(os.path.abspath(rel_to))
    
    # Split the paths into parts
    path_parts = path.strip(os.path.sep).split(os.path.sep)
    rel_to_parts = rel_to.strip(os.path.sep).split(os.path.sep)
    
    # Remove common prefix parts
    while path_parts and rel_to_parts and path_parts[0] == rel_to_parts[0]:
        path_parts.pop(0)
        rel_to_parts.pop(0)
    
    # Construct the relative path
    full_parts = ['..'] * len(rel_to_parts) + path_parts + [path_filename]
    if full_parts == ['']:
        return '.'
    return os.path.sep.join(full_parts)

def find_eggs_in_zip(importer, path_item, only=False):
    """
    Recursively finds eggs within a zip file.

    Args:
        importer (zipimport.zipimporter): The zipimporter object for the zip file.
        path_item (str): The path to the zip file.
        only (bool, optional): If True, only yields the top-level distribution. Defaults to False.

    Yields:
        Distribution: A distribution object representing an egg found within the zip file.
    """
    if importer.archive.endswith('.whl'):
        # Wheels are not supported and won't contain eggs
        return

    metadata = EggMetadata(importer)
    if metadata.has_metadata('PKG-INFO'):
        yield Distribution.from_filename(path_item, metadata=metadata)

    if only:
        # Don't yield nested distributions
        return

    for subitem in metadata.resource_listdir('/'):
        if subitem.endswith('.egg'):
            subpath = os.path.join(path_item, subitem)
            for dist in find_eggs_in_zip(zipimport.zipimporter(subpath), subpath):
                yield dist

    env = _markerlib.default_environment()
    
    # Translates keys in the environment from 'key.name' to 'key_name'.
    for key in env.keys():
        new_key = key.replace('.', '_')
        env[new_key] = env.pop(key)
    
    try:
        # Interprets the given text using the translated environment.
        result = _markerlib.interpret(text, env)

def scientific_notation_elements(self, value, locale):
    # Normalize the value to have only one leading digit.
    exp = value.adjusted()
    value = value * get_decimal_quantum(exp)
    assert value.adjusted() == 0  # Ensure the exponent is adjusted to 0.

    # Shift the exponent and value by the minimum number of leading digits
    # imposed by the rendering pattern, ensuring at least one leading digit.
    lead_shift = max([1, min(self.int_prec)]) - 1
    exp = exp - lead_shift
    value = value * get_decimal_quantum(-lead_shift)

    # Get the exponent sign symbol based on the exponent and locale settings.
    exp_sign = ''
    if exp < 0:
        exp_sign = babel.numbers.get_minus_sign_symbol(locale)
    elif self.exp_plus:
        exp_sign = babel.numbers.get_plus_sign_symbol(locale)

    # Normalize the exponent value now that the sign is determined.
    exp = abs(exp)

    return value, exp, exp_sign

def _get_unpatched(cls):
    """
    This function takes a class `cls` as input and iteratively checks its module name.
    If the module name starts with 'setuptools', it moves to the first base class of `cls`.
    This process continues until the module name does not start with 'setuptools'.
    If the module name starts with 'distutils' at any point, it raises an AssertionError
    indicating that 'distutils' has already been patched by the class `cls`.
    Finally, it returns the unpatched class.
    """
    while cls.__module__.startswith('setuptools'):
        cls, = cls.__bases__
    if cls.__module__.startswith('distutils'):
        raise AssertionError("distutils has already been patched by %r" % cls)
    return cls

def _build_editable_options(req):
    # Compile a regular expression to match query parameters in the request string.
    regexp = re.compile(r"[\?#&](?P<name>[^&=]+)=(?P<value>[^&=]+)")
    
    # Find all matches of the regular expression in the request string.
    matched = regexp.findall(req)
    
    # If matches are found, create a dictionary to store the options.
    if matched:
        ret = dict()
        
        # Iterate over each match.
        for option in matched:
            name, value = option
            
            # Check if the option name already exists in the dictionary.
            if name in ret:
                raise Exception("%s option already defined" % name)
            
            # Add the option to the dictionary.
            ret[name] = value
        
        # Return the dictionary of options.
        return ret
    
    # If no matches are found, return None.
    return None

def iri_to_uri(iri, charset='utf-8', errors='strict', safe_conversion=False):
    """
    Converts an Internationalized Resource Identifier (IRI) to a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI).

    Parameters:
    iri (str or tuple): The IRI to convert. If a tuple, it is first converted to a URL using `url_unparse`.
    charset (str): The character set to use for encoding. Default is 'utf-8'.
    errors (str): The error handling scheme. Default is 'strict'.
    safe_conversion (bool): If True, attempts to convert the IRI to ASCII and returns the native IRI if successful.

    Returns:
    str: The converted URI.
    """
    if isinstance(iri, tuple):
        iri = url_unparse(iri)

    if safe_conversion:
        try:
            native_iri = to_native(iri)
            ascii_iri = to_native(iri).encode('ascii')
            if ascii_iri.split() == [ascii_iri]:
                return native_iri
        except UnicodeError:
            pass

    iri = url_parse(to_unicode(iri, charset, errors))
    netloc = iri.encode_netloc()
    path = url_quote(iri.path, charset, errors, '/:~+%')
    query = url_quote(iri.query, charset, errors, '%&[]:;$*()+,!?*/=')
    fragment = url_quote(iri.fragment, charset, errors, '=%&[]:;$()+,!?*/')

    return to_native(url_unparse((iri.scheme, netloc, path, query, fragment)))

def Popen_nonblocking(*args, **kwargs):
    kwargs.setdefault('close_fds', 'posix' in sys.builtin_module_names)
    kwargs.setdefault('bufsize', 1)
    proc = subprocess.Popen(*args, **kwargs)
    
    if proc.stdout:
        q = queue.Queue()
        t = threading.Thread(target=enqueue_lines, args=(proc.stdout, q))
        proc.stdout = q
        t.daemon = True
        t.start()
    
    if proc.stderr:
        q = queue.Queue()
        t = threading.Thread(target=enqueue_lines, args=(proc.stderr, q))
        proc.stderr = q
        t.daemon = True
        t.start()
    
    return proc


**Summary:**
The `Popen_nonblocking` function is designed to create a non-blocking subprocess using the `subprocess.Popen` method. It sets default values for `close_fds` and `bufsize` in the `kwargs` dictionary. If the subprocess has a standard output (`stdout`), it creates a queue and a daemon thread to enqueue lines from the output. Similarly, if the subprocess has a standard error (`stderr`), it creates another queue and daemon thread to enqueue lines from the error. def _download_http_url(link, session, temp_dir):
    """
    Downloads a file from a given HTTP URL using the provided session and saves it to a temporary directory.

    Args:
        link (object): An object containing the URL to download.
        session (object): A session object used to make HTTP requests.
        temp_dir (str): The path to the temporary directory where the file will be saved.

    Returns:
        tuple: A tuple containing the file path and content type of the downloaded file.

    Raises:
        requests.HTTPError: If an HTTP error occurs during the download.
    """
    target_url = link.url.split('#', 1)[0]
    try:
        resp = session.get(target_url, headers={"Accept-Encoding": "identity"}, stream=True)
        resp.raise_for_status()
    except requests.HTTPError as exc:
        logger.critical("HTTP error %s while getting %s", exc.response.status_code, link)
        raise

    content_type = resp.headers.get('content-type', '')
    filename = link.filename
    content_disposition = resp.headers.get('content-disposition')
    if content_disposition:
        type, params = cgi.parse_header(content_disposition)
        filename = params.get('filename') or filename
    ext = os.path.splitext(filename)[1]
    if not ext:
        ext = mimetypes.guess_extension(content_type)
    if ext:
        filename += ext
    if not ext and link.url != resp.url:
        ext = os.path.splitext(resp.url)[1]
        if ext:
            filename += ext
    file_path = os.path.join(temp_dir, filename)
    with open(file_path, 'wb') as content_file:
        _download_url(resp, link, content_file)
    return file_path, content_type

def visit_Include(self, node, frame):
    if node.with_context:
        self.unoptimize_scope(frame)
    if node.ignore_missing:
        self.writeline('try:')
        self.indent()
    func_name = 'get_or_select_template'
    if isinstance(node.template, nodes.Const):
        if isinstance(node.template.value, string_types):
            func_name = 'get_template'
        elif isinstance(node.template.value, (tuple, list)):
            func_name = 'select_template'
    elif isinstance(node.template, (nodes.Tuple, nodes.List)):
        func_name = 'select_template'
    self.writeline('template = environment.%s(' % func_name, node)
    self.visit(node.template, frame)
    self.write(', %r)' % self.name)
    if node.ignore_missing:
        self.outdent()
        self.writeline('except TemplateNotFound:')
        self.indent()
        self.writeline('pass')
        self.outdent()
    self.writeline('else:')
    self.indent()
    if node.with_context:
        self.writeline('for event in template.root_render_func('
                      'template.new_context(context.parent, True, '
                      'locals())):')
    else:
        self.writeline('for event in template.module._body_stream:')
    self.indent()
    self.simple_write('event', frame)
    self.outdent()
    if node.ignore_missing:
        self.outdent()

def _safe_get_element(self, path, root=None):
    """
    Safely retrieves an element from a nested structure using a dot-separated path.
    
    Args:
        path (str): The dot-separated path to the desired element.
        root (object, optional): The root object from which to start the search. If None, the search starts from `self.item`.
    
    Returns:
        object: The element at the specified path, or None if the path is invalid or the element does not exist.
    """
    elements = path.split('.')
    parent = root if root is not None else self.item
    for element in elements[:-1]:
        parent = getattr(parent, element, None)
        if parent is None:
            return None
    return getattr(parent, elements[-1], None)

    # Convert signed_value and self.sep to bytes
    signed_value = want_bytes(signed_value)
    sep = want_bytes(self.sep)
    
    # Check if separator is in signed_value
    if sep not in signed_value:
        raise BadSignature('No %r found in value' % self.sep)
    
    # Split signed_value into value and signature
    value, sig = signed_value.rsplit(sep, 1)
    
    # Verify the signature

    else:
        raise BadSignature('Signature %r does not match' % sig, payload=value)

def create(self, prog=None, format=None):
    # Set default values for program and format if not provided
    prog = self.program if prog is None else prog
    format = self.format if format is None else format
    
    # Create a temporary file
    tmp_fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(tmp_fd)
    
    # Save the graph to the temporary file
    dot_fd = open(tmp_name, "w+b")
    self.save_dot(dot_fd)
    dot_fd.close()
    
    # Get the temporary file directory
    tmp_dir = os.path.dirname(tmp_name)
    
    # Process the file using the layout program, specifying the format
    p = subprocess.Popen((self.programs[prog], '-T' + format, tmp_name), cwd=tmp_dir, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
    
    # Read the standard output and standard error from the process
    stdout_output = []
    while True:
        data = p.stdout.read()
        if not data:
            break
        stdout_output.append(data)
    p.stdout.close()
    stdout_output = ''.join(stdout_output) if stdout_output else None
    
    stderr_output = []
    while True:
        data = p.stderr.read()
        if not data:
            break
        stderr_output.append(data)
    p.stderr.close()
    stderr_output = ''.join(stderr_output) if stderr_output else None
    
    # Wait for the process to complete and check the status
    status = p.wait()
    if status != 0:
        logger.error("Program terminated with status: %d. stderr follows: %s" % (status, stderr_output))
    elif stderr_output:
        logger.error("%s", stderr_output)
    
    # Remove the temporary file
    os.unlink(tmp_name)
    
    return stdout_output

def add_subgraph(self, subgraph_or_ID):
    """
    Adds a subgraph or cluster to the current graph.

    Parameters:
    subgraph_or_ID (godot.subgraph.Subgraph, godot.cluster.Cluster, str): The subgraph or cluster to add, or its ID as a string.

    Returns:
    godot.subgraph.Subgraph or godot.cluster.Cluster: The added subgraph or cluster.

    Raises:
    ValueError: If the input is not a valid subgraph, cluster, or string ID.
    """
    if not isinstance(subgraph_or_ID, (godot.subgraph.Subgraph, godot.cluster.Cluster)):
        subgraphID = str(subgraph_or_ID)
        if subgraphID.startswith("cluster"):
            subgraph = godot.cluster.Cluster(ID=subgraphID)
        else:
            subgraph = godot.subgraph.Subgraph(ID=subgraphID)
    else:
        subgraph = subgraph_or_ID

    subgraph.default_node = self.default_node
    subgraph.default_edge = self.default_edge
    # subgraph.level = self.level + 1
    # subgraph.padding += self.padding

    if isinstance(subgraph, godot.subgraph.Subgraph):
        self.subgraphs.append(subgraph)
    elif isinstance(subgraph, godot.cluster.Cluster):
        self.clusters.append(subgraph)
    else:
        raise ValueError("Invalid input type")

    return subgraph

def windows(iterable, length=2, overlap=0, padding=True):
    it = iter(iterable)
    results = list(itertools.islice(it, length))
    while len(results) == length:
        yield results
        results = results[length - overlap:]
        results.extend(itertools.islice(it, length - overlap))
    if padding and results:
        results.extend(itertools.repeat(None, length - len(results)))
    yield results

def _on_drawing(self, object, name, old, new):
    # Define attributes to consider
    attrs = ["drawing", "arrowhead_drawing"]
    
    # Get other drawing objects and their positions relative to the current object
    others = [getattr(self, a) for a in attrs if a != name and getattr(self, a) is not None]
    x, y = self.component.position
    abs_x = [d.x + x for d in others]
    abs_y = [d.y + y for d in others]
    
    # Calculate the new position for the drawing object relative to the graph origin
    x1 = min(abs_x + [new.x])
    y1 = min(abs_y + [new.y])
    new.position = [new.x - x1, new.y - y1]
    
    # Update the positions of other drawing objects relative to the new origin
    for i, b in enumerate(others):
        b.position = [abs_x[i] - x1, abs_y[i] - y1]
    
    # Remove the old drawing object and add the new one
    if old is not None:
        self.component.remove(old)
    if new is not None:
        self.component.add(new)
    
    # Update the component's position and request a redraw

def _draw_mainlayer(self, gc, view_bounds=None, mode="default"):
    if not self.points:
        return gc.save_state()
    try:
        gc.set_fill_color(self.pen.fill_color_)
        gc.set_line_width(self.pen.line_width)
        gc.set_stroke_color(self.pen.color_)
        gc.begin_path()
        start_x, start_y = self.points[0]
        gc.move_to(start_x, start_y)
        for triple in nsplit(self.points[1:], 3):
            x1, y1 = triple[0]
            x2, y2 = triple[1]
            end_x, end_y = triple[2]
            gc.curve_to(x1, y1, x2, y2, end_x, end_y)
            gc.move_to(end_x, end_y)
        gc.stroke_path()
    finally:
        gc.restore_state()

It then begins a path and moves to the starting point. For each set of three points (representing a cubic Bézier curve), it calculates the control points and draws the curve. After drawing all curves, it moves to the end point of the last curve. Finally, it strokes the path and restores the graphics context to its previous state.

def _normalize_host(host, enable_long_host=False, encode_with_idna=None, scheme=None):
    """
    Normalize the given host by encoding it with IDNA if specified, and then quoting it with UTF-8.
    If the host is too long and long hosts are not enabled, raise a ValueError.
    
    Args:
    host (str): The host to be normalized.
    enable_long_host (bool, optional): Whether to allow long hosts. Defaults to False.
    encode_with_idna (bool, optional): Whether to encode the host with IDNA. Defaults to None.
    scheme (str, optional): The scheme of the URL. Defaults to None.
    
    Returns:
    str: The normalized host.
    
    Raises:
    ValueError: If the host is invalid or too long and long hosts are not enabled.
    """
    if encode_with_idna is not None:
        enable_idna = encode_with_idna
    else:
        enable_idna = scheme.lower() in IDNA_SCHEMES if scheme else False
    
    if enable_idna:
        try:
            host = '.'.join(segment.encode('idna').decode() for segment in host.split('.'))
        except UnicodeError as exc:
            raise ValueError(f'host is invalid - {exc}')
    
    host = parse.quote(host.encode('utf-8'), safe=HOST_SAFE_CHARS)
    
    if len(host) > 255 and not enable_long_host:
        raise ValueError('host too long')
    
    return host

def luhn_check(card_number):
    sum = 0
    num_digits = len(card_number)
    oddeven = num_digits & 1
    for count in range(num_digits):
        digit = int(card_number[count])
        if not ((count & 1) ^ oddeven):
            digit *= 2
            if digit > 9:
                digit -= 9
        sum += digit
    return (sum % 10) == 0


**Summary:**
The `luhn_check` function implements the Luhn algorithm to validate a credit card number. It iterates through each digit of the card number, doubles every second digit from the right (considering the rightmost digit as the first), and subtracts 9 from any doubled digit that is greater than 9. It then sums all the digits and checks if the total modulo 10 is zero, indicating a valid card number.

def find_module(self, module_name, path=None):
    # Join the module name parts with the module path separator
    module_path = os.path.join(*module_name.split(MODULE_PATH_SEP))
    
    # Iterate through each search root in the paths list
    for search_root in self.paths:
        # Construct the target path by joining the search root and module path
        target_path = os.path.join(search_root, module_path)
        
        # Initialize a flag to check if the target is a package
        is_pkg = False
        
        # Check if the target path is a directory
        if os.path.isdir(target_path):
            # If it is a directory, try to load it as a package by referencing the __init__.py file
            target_file = os.path.join(target_path, '__init__.py')
            is_pkg = True
        else:
            # If it is not a directory, append .py and attempt to resolve it
            target_file = '{}.py'.format(target_path)
        
        # Check if the target file exists
        if os.path.exists(target_file):
            # Return a ModuleLoader object with the target path, module name, target file, and package flag
            return ModuleLoader(target_path, module_name, target_file, is_pkg)
    
    # Return None if no module is found
    return None

def get(self, k, wait=False, wait_index=False, timeout='5m'):
    """
    Fetches the value associated with the given key from the key-value store.

    Args:
        k (str): The key to fetch.
        wait (bool, optional): Whether to wait for the key to be available. Defaults to False.
        wait_index (bool, optional): The index to wait for if wait is True. Defaults to False.
        timeout (str, optional): The timeout duration for the wait operation. Defaults to '5m'.

    Returns:
        bytes: The value associated with the key, decoded from base64.

    Raises:
        KeyDoesNotExist: If the key does not exist in the store.
        KVStoreError: If the GET request returns a status code other than 200.
    """
    k = k.lstrip('/')
    url = '{}/{}'.format(self.endpoint, k)
    params = {}
    if wait:
        params['index'] = wait_index
        params['wait'] = timeout
    r = requests.get(url, params=params)
    if r.status_code == 404:
        raise KeyDoesNotExist("Key " + k + " does not exist")
    if r.status_code != 200:
        raise KVStoreError('GET returned {}'.format(r.status_code))
    try:
        return base64.b64decode(r.json()[0]['Value'])
    except TypeError as e:
        return ""

def recurse(self, k, wait=False, wait_index=None, timeout='5m'):
    """
    Recursively retrieves entries from a key-value store.

    Args:
        k (str): The key to retrieve.
        wait (bool, optional): Whether to wait for the key to be available. Defaults to False.
        wait_index (int, optional): The index to wait for. Defaults to None.
        timeout (str, optional): The timeout duration. Defaults to '5m'.

    Returns:
        dict: A dictionary of entries retrieved from the key-value store.

    Raises:
        KeyDoesNotExist: If the key does not exist.
        KVStoreError: If the GET request returns a non-200 status code.
    """
    k = k.lstrip('/')
    url = '{}/{}'.format(self.endpoint, k)
    params = {}
    params['recurse'] = 'true'
    if wait:
        params['wait'] = timeout
    if not wait_index:
        params['index'] = self.index(k, recursive=True)
    else:
        params['index'] = wait_index
    r = requests.get(url, params=params)
    if r.status_code == 404:
        raise KeyDoesNotExist("Key " + k + " does not exist")
    if r.status_code != 200:
        raise KVStoreError('GET returned {}'.format(r.status_code))
    entries = {}
    for e in r.json():
        if e['Value']:
            entries[e['Key']] = base64.b64decode(e['Value'])
        else:
            entries[e['Key']] = ''
    return entries

def feature_importance_report(X, y, threshold=0.001, correcting_multiple_hypotheses=True, method='fdr_bh', alpha=0.1, sort_by='pval'):
    """
    Generates a feature importance report for a given dataset.

    Parameters:
    - X: Feature matrix.
    - y: Target vector.
    - threshold: Variance threshold for feature selection.
    - correcting_multiple_hypotheses: Boolean indicating whether to correct for multiple hypotheses.
    - method: Method for multiple hypothesis correction.
    - alpha: Significance level for multiple hypothesis correction.
    - sort_by: Column to sort the results by.

    Returns:
    - A DataFrame containing feature importance metrics.
    """
    # Apply variance thresholding to the feature matrix
    df = variance_threshold_on_df(pd.DataFrame.from_records(X), threshold=threshold)
    
    # Perform ANOVA F-test
    F, pvals = f_classif(df.values, y)
    
    # Correct for multiple hypotheses if required
    if correcting_multiple_hypotheses:
        _, pvals, _, _ = multipletests(pvals, alpha=alpha, method=method)
    
    # Add target labels to the DataFrame
    df['labels'] = y
    
    # Calculate mean values for each label
    df_mean = df.groupby('labels').mean().T
    
    # Add F-statistic and p-values to the DataFrame
    df_mean['F'] = F
    df_mean['pval'] = pvals
    
    # Sort the DataFrame by the specified column
    return df_mean.sort_values(sort_by, ascending=True)

    if os.path.splitext(file_name)[1] == '.mp3':
        log.info(f"{file_name} is already a MP3 file, no conversion needed.")
        return file_name
    
    # Create a new MP3 file name
    new_file_name = os.path.splitext(file_name)[0] + '.mp3'
    
    # Initialize FFmpeg for conversion
    ff = FFmpeg(inputs={file_name: None}, outputs={new_file_name: None})
    log.info(f"Conversion for {file_name} has started")
    
    # Start the conversion process
    start_time = time()
    try:
        ff.run(stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    except FFRuntimeError:
        # Remove the partially created MP3 file if conversion fails
        os.remove(new_file_name)
        ff.run(stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
    
    # Log the completion of the conversion
    end_time = time()
    log.info(f"Conversion for {file_name} has finished in {end_time - start_time} seconds")
    
    # Add the original file to the delete queue
    delete_queue.put(file_name)
    
    # Return the new MP3 file name
    return new_file_name

def init_celery(app, celery):
    # Update the Celery configuration with the Flask app's configuration
    celery.conf.update(app.config)
    
    # Define an abstract base class for Celery tasks that uses the Flask app context
    class ContextTask(celery.Task):
        abstract = True
        
        def __call__(self, *args, **kwargs):
            with app.app_context():
                return super().__call__(*args, **kwargs)
    
    # Replace the default Celery Task class with the ContextTask
    celery.Task = ContextTask
    
    # Return the modified Celery instance
    return celery

def parse_accept(header_value):
    """
    Parses the 'Accept' header value and returns a list of parsed headers with their qualities.

    :param str header_value: The 'Accept' header value to parse.
    :return: A list of parsed headers with their qualities.
    :rtype: list
    """
    next_explicit_q = decimal.ExtendedContext.next_plus(decimal.Decimal('5.0'))
    headers = [parse_content_type(header) for header in parse_list(header_value)]
    for header in headers:
        q = header.parameters.pop('q', None)
        if q is None:
            q = '1.0'
        elif float(q) == 1.0:
            q = float(next_explicit_q)
        next_explicit_q = next_explicit_q.next_minus()
        header.quality = float(q)
    return sorted(headers, key=functools.cmp_to_key(ordering))

def ordering(left, right):
    """
    Method for sorting the header values based on their quality.

    :param mixed left: The left header to compare.
    :param mixed right: The right header to compare.
    :return: The result of the comparison.
    :rtype: int
    """
    if left.quality != right.quality:
        return right.quality - left.quality
    if left == right:
        return 0
    if left > right:
        return -1
    return 1

def parse_content_type(content_type, normalize_parameter_values=True):
    # Remove comments from the content type string
    parts = _remove_comments(content_type).split(';')
    
    # Split the content type into main type and subtype
    content_type, content_subtype = parts.pop(0).split('/')
    
    # Handle subtype suffix if present
    if '+' in content_subtype:
        content_subtype, content_suffix = content_subtype.split('+')
    else:
        content_suffix = None
    
    # Parse parameters and normalize their values if required
    parameters = _parse_parameter_list(parts, normalize_parameter_values=normalize_parameter_values)
    
    # Return a ContentType object with parsed data
    return datastructures.ContentType(content_type, content_subtype, dict(parameters), content_suffix)

def _read_iop_from_file(self, file_name):
    """
    Reads IOP data from a CSV file and interpolates it to a common wavelength grid.

    Args:
        file_name (str): The path to the CSV file containing IOP data.

    Returns:
        float or numpy.ndarray: Interpolated IOP values at the common wavelength grid, or -1 if an error occurs.

    Raises:
        IOError: If the file cannot be read or if there is an error during interpolation.
    """
    lg.info(f'Reading :: {file_name} :: and interpolating to {self.wavelengths}')
    if os.path.isfile(file_name):
        with open(file_name, 'r') as file:
            iop_reader = csv.reader(file, delimiter=',', quotechar='"')
            wave = next(iop_reader)
            iop = next(iop_reader)
    else:
        lg.exception(f'Problem reading file :: {file_name}')
        raise IOError

    try:
        wave = list(map(float, wave))
        iop = list(map(float, iop))
        return scipy.interp(self.wavelengths, wave, iop)
    except IOError:
        lg.exception('Error interpolating IOP to common wavelength')
        return -1

def fetch_metric(self, metric, start, end, tags={}, aggregator="sum", downsample=None, ms_resolution=True):
    """
    Fetches a metric from a data source within a specified time range and with optional tags, aggregation, and downsampling.

    Parameters:
    - metric (str): The name of the metric to fetch.
    - start (datetime): The start time of the time range.
    - end (datetime): The end time of the time range.
    - tags (dict, optional): A dictionary of tags to filter the metric data. Defaults to an empty dictionary.
    - aggregator (str, optional): The aggregation function to apply. Defaults to "sum".
    - downsample (str, optional): The downsampling interval. If provided, it should be in the format "Xs" (e.g., "1m" for 1 minute). Defaults to None.
    - ms_resolution (bool, optional): Whether to use millisecond resolution. Defaults to True.

    Returns:
    - dict: The fetched metric data, or an empty dictionary if no data is available.

    Raises:
    - QueryError: If the request to the data source fails.
    """
    query = "{aggregator}:{downsample}{metric}{{{tags}}}".format(
        aggregator=aggregator,
        downsample=downsample + "-avg:" if downsample else "",
        metric=metric,
        tags=','.join("%s=%s" % (k, v) for k, v in tags.items())
    )
    params = {
        'ms': ms_resolution,
        'start': '{0:.3f}'.format(start.timestamp()),
        'end': '{0:.3f}'.format(end.timestamp()),
        'm': query
    }
    response = self.__request("/query", params)
    if response.status_code == 200:
        try:
            return response.json()[0]['dps']
        except IndexError:  # empty data set
            return {}
    raise QueryError(response.json())

def __sig_from_func(self, func):
    # Determine if the function is a method or a regular function
    if isinstance(func, types.MethodType):
        # For bound instance or class methods
        argspec = getfullargspec(func.__func__)
        self.pargl = argspec[0][1:]
    else:
        # For regular functions, unbound instance methods, or bound static methods
        argspec = getfullargspec(func)
        self.pargl = argspec[0][:]
    
    # Handle default arguments
    if argspec[3] is not None:
        def_offset = len(self.pargl) - len(argspec[3])
        self.def_argv = dict((self.pargl[def_offset + i], argspec[3][i]) for i in range(len(argspec[3])))
    else:
        self.def_argv = {}
    
    # Determine if the function has variable positional and keyword arguments
    self.var_pargs = argspec[1] is not None
    self.var_kargs = argspec[2] is not None
    
    # Handle keyword-only arguments
    self.kargl = argspec[4]
    if argspec[5] is not None:
        self.def_argv.update(argspec[5])

def vlq2int(data):
    # Initialize the value and shift counter
    value = 0
    shift = 0
    
    # Read bytes from the data until the most significant bit is not set
    while True:
        byte = ord(data.read(1))
        value |= (byte & 0x7F) << (shift * 7)
        shift += 1
        if byte & 0x80 == 0:
            break
    
    return value

def get_duration(self, seconds):
    duration = ""
    minutes, seconds = divmod(seconds, 60)
    if minutes >= 60:
        hours, minutes = divmod(minutes, 60)
        duration = "%sh " % hours
    duration += "%sm %ss" % (minutes, seconds)
    return duration

    the_file_name = str(self.result_file)
    the_file = open(the_file_name, 'r')
    lines = the_file.readlines()

    # Split each line into cells and store in a 2D array
    lines_array = []
    for line in lines:
        line = line.split(',')
        lines_array.append(line)

    labels_line = lines_array[0]
    cell_labels_line = 0
    flag = True

    # Find the index of the 'wavelength' label
    try:
        while flag:
            if 'wavelength (nm)' in labels_line[cell_labels_line]:
                index = labels_line.index(labels_line[cell_labels_line])
                flag = False
            else:
                cell_labels_line += 1
    except IndexError:
        raise sys.exit("Warning: There is no value named 'wavelength' in the file used to plot curves. So, I can't separate data to plot curves and data about tests linking with these curves.")

    self.information = []
    data_wavelength = []
    self.num_line = 0

    # Separate data into information and wavelength arrays
    for line in lines_array:
        cell_line = 0
        self.information.append([])
        data_wavelength.append([])
        while cell_line < len(line):
            if cell_line < index:
                self.information[self.num_line].append(line[cell_line])
            elif cell_line > index:
                data_wavelength[self.num_line].append(line[cell_line])
            cell_line += 1
        self.num_line += 1

    # Convert wavelength data to floats
    line_wavelength = 0
    for row_data_wavelength in data_wavelength:
        row_data_wavelength = [float(item.strip('\n').strip('\"')) for item in row_data_wavelength]

        line_wavelength += 1

    self.wavelength = data_wavelength[0]  # The first line contains wavelength

    the_file.close()

def sign(self, privkey):
    if self.v:
        raise InvalidSignature("already signed")
    if privkey in (0, '', '\x00' * 32):
        raise InvalidSignature("Zero privkey cannot sign")
    rawhash = sha3(rlp.encode(self, self.__class__.exclude(['v', 'r', 's'])))
    if len(privkey) == 64:
        privkey = encode_privkey(privkey, 'bin')
    pk = PrivateKey(privkey, raw=True)
    signature = pk.ecdsa_recoverable_serialize(pk.ecdsa_sign_recoverable(rawhash, raw=True))
    signature = signature[0] + chr(signature[1])
    self.v = ord(signature[64]) + 27
    self.r = big_endian_to_int(signature[0:32])
    self.s = big_endian_to_int(signature[32:64])
    self._sender = None
    return self

def img_to_vgg(x):
    # Convert image from RGB to BGR
    x = x[:, :, ::-1]
    # Subtract mean values for each channel
    x[:, :, 0] -= 103.939
    x[:, :, 1] -= 116.779
    x[:, :, 2] -= 123.68
    # Transpose the image dimensions to (channels, height, width)
    x = x.transpose((2, 0, 1))
    return x
